scope: First-run setup, saved settings and packaged native startup
coverage_policy: Passed fixture results prove only their stated fixture behavior. Native smoke under Wine is distinct from physical Windows, audible device output and complete gameplay parity.

automated: Tkinter and a display server for GUI cases
runtime: The native build or extracted app package
A legally owned supported game ISO or installed assets
Private writable settings, asset cache and test save directories

scenarios.title: Import a supported disc on first start
setup: Use a fresh per-user configuration and asset cache.
Use a legally owned supported PC disc ISO.
steps: Open OpenSpidey without arguments.
Choose the ISO through the native file dialog.
Visit Game files, Video, Sound and Controls.
Choose output size and volume, then press Start.
Wait for import progress and launch.
expected: Setup appears before the first game run.
All four required files are imported to a writable cache.
Progress completes before preferences are saved or the game starts.
The ISO is not mounted, modified, or included in a release.
The game receives the saved settings.

verification.method: real Linux source GUI and frozen Windows GUI under Wine

scenarios.title: Validate an existing installed game folder
setup: Prepare a supported writable game folder and separate missing, damaged and read-only fixtures.
steps: Choose the installed-folder source option.
Select each fixture and press Start.
Finally select the valid folder.
expected: Invalid folders report the missing, damaged or non-writable requirement.
Invalid selections do not save settings or start a child.
The valid folder becomes the game working directory.

scenarios.title: Read ISO9660 and Joliet file trees
setup: Use synthetic ISO9660 and Joliet discs with the required four payloads.
steps: Inspect each disc.
Import each disc to a new cache.
Validate the imported folder and manifest.
expected: Both supported directory formats locate the same required files.
Imported payloads match the fixtures byte for byte and are writable.
Manifest records four SHA256 values.
Progress is monotonic and ends at the expected byte count.

scenarios.title: Reject truncated and malformed disc structures
setup: Use synthetic corrupt descriptors, extents, directory records and names.
steps: Try truncated images, conflicting endian sizes, out-of-range extents, short records, duplicate names and directory cycles.
Try unsupported multi-extent files and path separators in names.
expected: Each malformed image fails with an asset error.
No completed destination or launch is created.

scenarios.title: Reject an unsupported executable or invalid PKR
setup: Use synthetic missing-file, changed-executable and invalid-PKR fixtures.
steps: Inspect each fixture before import.
Check PKR magic, counts and payload bounds.
expected: The supported executable identity is required.
Missing assets and invalid archive structure are rejected before launching.

scenarios.title: Handle insufficient space and concurrent imports
setup: Use a private temporary destination with disk-space and lock fixtures.
steps: Report zero free space during import.
Hold the destination import lock and attempt another import.
Attempt an ISO located inside the destination; on Linux also try a symlink destination.
expected: A useful error is returned for each invalid condition.
No second import overwrites the active cache.
The source cannot be overwritten by its own import.

scenarios.title: Cancel import without losing an existing cache
setup: Prepare a valid cache and saved settings, then force another import.
steps: Cancel before copying starts.
Cancel again after a progress event.
Close the setup window while the import worker is active.
expected: The previous manifest and cache remain intact.
Temporary import files are cleaned up.
Settings are not overwritten and no child starts.
The GUI waits for the worker to acknowledge cancellation.

scenarios.title: Detect a disc changed while importing
setup: Prepare a valid cache and force reimport from a synthetic ISO.
steps: Change the ISO modification time during a progress callback.
Inspect the cache manifest afterward.
expected: Import fails because the source changed.
The previous completed cache is preserved.

scenarios.title: Reuse verified assets and repair a damaged cache
setup: Import a valid disc once.
steps: Import the same unchanged source again.
Confirm unchanged assets are not recopied.
Damage an imported asset and retry the import.
expected: A valid cache is reused.
A damaged asset is detected and restored from the disc.
Real Windows import also preserves an existing saved payload on cache reuse.

verification.method: synthetic tests and real supported ISO under Windows Wine

scenarios.title: Refresh assets without deleting saves
setup: Prepare an imported cache containing save/SPIDRMAN.DAT.
steps: Change the source fingerprint and reimport.
Compare the saved payload before and afterward.
expected: The manifest adopts the changed source fingerprint.
Existing saved progress remains byte identical.

scenarios.title: Start from a valid cache after the ISO is moved
setup: Save setup with a valid imported game cache and then make the ISO path unavailable.
steps: Reopen setup.
Press Start without choosing the ISO again.
expected: A validated completed cache can launch without the original ISO path.
No new import is attempted.

scenarios.title: Save preferences atomically and recover invalid settings
setup: Use a private per-user settings file.
steps: Round-trip display and source preferences.
Replace the file with invalid JSON.
Simulate a failure during atomic replacement.
expected: Valid preferences round-trip exactly.
Broken settings return safe defaults with a warning.
Failed saves retain the old file and leave no temporary settings file.

scenarios.title: Keep invalid settings out of the native game
setup: Prepare out-of-range settings and conflicting inherited environment variables.
steps: Load an unknown window mode, invalid resolution, boolean MSAA, NaN sensitivity and invalid volume.
Build the child environment from normalized values.
expected: Resolution, sample count and sensitivity recover to supported values.
Volumes are bounded to zero through one hundred.
Unsupported settings schema is rejected.
Saved preferences control the child environment; stale legacy flags do not override them.

scenarios.title: Skip setup after successful configuration
setup: Complete setup and save a valid cache with show_setup disabled.
steps: Close the game.
Open OpenSpidey again without arguments.
Exit the child with F12.
expected: The saved game starts without an extra setup window.
The child receives one game-directory argument and does not recursively open setup.
A successful child exit returns code zero.

verification.method: real Linux source GUI and frozen Windows app under Wine

scenarios.title: Reopen setup from the Settings shortcut
setup: Complete setup with non-default video preferences.
steps: Open OpenSpidey-Settings on Linux or OpenSpidey Settings.exe on Windows.
Visit Video and inspect saved values.
Change one preference and start again.
expected: The shortcut opens setup even when normal launches autostart.
Saved preferences are displayed.
The child uses the newly saved setting.

verification.method: real frozen Linux and Windows GUI under Wine

scenarios.title: Import and launch from non-ASCII Windows paths
setup: Use an import destination containing an accent, Chinese characters and an emoji.
steps: Import the real supported ISO.
Save settings with the Unicode cache folder.
Autostart the frozen app and run the native save fixture from that working directory.
expected: All four asset hashes match the known supported disc.
The child working directory is preserved.
Native save write and read round-trip the fixture bytes.

verification.method: real Windows frozen app and native save fixture under Wine

scenarios.title: Create and read native backup saves
setup: Build tests/platform/save_paths.cpp with the real native save routines.
Use a private writable working directory.
steps: Run with no save directory.
Create, write, close and reopen a fixture save.
Check callbacks, invalid handles and error returns.
expected: The native save directory is created.
A 512-byte payload round-trips.
Callbacks and error return values satisfy the fixture.
The Windows case additionally covers ASCII and Unicode working directories.

verification.method: native Linux and Windows save fixtures

scenarios.title: Resize a window while preserving the game aspect ratio
setup: Run tests/platform/setup_sdl.cpp on a 1920x1080 X11 display with a window manager and dummy audio.
steps: Request a 1280x720 output window with four samples.
Read the GL viewport and check border pixels.
Capture the logical 640x480 frame.
Resize the output to 640x360 and redraw.
expected: The initial viewport is 160,0,960,720.
The resized viewport is 80,0,480,360.
Borders remain black and both scene and movie occupy the 4:3 viewport.
Logical capture includes the game view without the outer bars.

scenarios.title: Use desktop borderless fullscreen
setup: Use the same SDL fixture on a 1920x1080 desktop.
steps: Request borderless mode.
Check SDL fullscreen flags and selected fullscreen mode.
Check the drawable viewport and movie pixels.
expected: The window occupies the desktop without an exclusive display mode.
Output is 1920x1080 with viewport 240,0,1440,1080.
Scene, movie and capture preserve 4:3.

scenarios.title: Select a supported exclusive fullscreen mode
setup: Use the same SDL fixture with a reported 1920x1080 display mode.
steps: Request fullscreen at 1920x1080.
Check the selected SDL display mode and fullscreen flags.
Read the game viewport.
expected: The requested exclusive mode is selected.
Output is 1920x1080 with viewport 240,0,1440,1080.
A zero reported refresh rate is never used as a divisor.

scenarios.title: Recover from unsupported fullscreen and antialiasing
setup: Use the same SDL fixture where 1280x720 exclusive mode and sixteen samples are unavailable.
steps: Request the unavailable exclusive mode.
Separately request sixteen MSAA samples.
Check actual output mode, sample count and warnings.
expected: Unsupported exclusive mode falls back to desktop borderless.
Unsupported MSAA retries with zero samples and creates a working context.
The log reports requested failures and actual settings.
Both fallbacks still pass scene, movie, capture and audio gain checks.

scenarios.title: Verify supported vertical synchronization
setup: Use a physical monitor and driver which support swap interval changes.
steps: Enable vsync in setup and start the game.
Inspect the actual reported swap interval and frame presentation.
Disable vsync and repeat.
expected: Supported settings match the requested swap interval.
Unsupported drivers report the failure and actual interval.
Pacing and tearing are assessed on the physical display.

verification.method: physical display check required; Xvfb reported unsupported vsync

scenarios.title: Apply master, music and effects settings to actual SDL streams
setup: Run tests/platform/setup_sdl.cpp with SDL dummy audio.
steps: Set master to forty percent, effects to twenty-five and music to fifty.
Open effects, music and movie streams.
Change per-stream music and movie volume.
Mute master and repeat the music and movie volume calls.
expected: Effects stream gain is 0.1 and music initial gain is 0.2.
Movie initial gain is 0.4.
Per-stream volume multiplies the saved master/channel gains.
Master mute produces zero music and movie gains.
This verifies sink settings without claiming audible device output.

scenarios.title: Listen to dialogue, effects and movies on a real output device
setup: Use working speakers or headphones and a supported physical audio device.
steps: Compare master, Music and voices, and Sound effects at zero, fifty and one hundred.
Play menu music, dialogue, a movie and repeated game effects.
Change the default output device between launches.
expected: Each channel responds independently to its setup setting.
Master affects all channels.
No clipping, stale stream, missing dialogue or accumulating delay is heard.
A missing device fails gracefully.

verification.method: physical audio check required; setup runtime smoke used mute or dummy audio

scenarios.title: Verify mouse direction, sensitivity and action bindings
setup: Configure modern controls and enter a safe section of level 1.
steps: Test mouse look horizontally and vertically at two sensitivity settings.
Toggle vertical inversion through Settings and repeat.
Test movement, jump, punch and web bindings.
Compare the same route with modern controls disabled.
expected: Camera direction follows the configured inversion and sensitivity.
Bindings trigger the expected actions without rotation drift or a crash.
A short scripted key attempt alone does not prove attack visibility, collision or damage.

verification.method: preferences automated; complete gameplay assessment still required

scenarios.title: Render a movie in the selected viewport and skip with Escape
setup: Use a legally owned game cache with movies enabled.
For aspect checks also run the SDL movie framebuffer fixture.
steps: Start a movie from a saved launcher configuration.
Inspect its viewport and border pixels in the fixture.
Press Escape using native game input.
Press F12 to finish the bounded run.
expected: Movie output preserves the game aspect ratio.
Escape returns from playback.
F12 returns a successful child exit in the tested Windows Wine run.
The movie decoder is packaged rather than depending on an external Bink DLL.

verification.method: Linux SDL movie pixels and frozen Windows movie/keyboard smoke under Wine

scenarios.title: Report a child failure with a persistent log
setup: Use a private fixture executable that exits with a nonzero code.
steps: Start the fixture through the launcher.
Read the displayed error and its log location.
Repeat with a missing game executable.
expected: The launcher does not report a failed child as successful.
Stdout and stderr persist in a per-user log.
The error dialog identifies the exit code and log.
Missing executable produces a useful dialog before launching.

verification.method: Linux process fixture and real frozen Windows error dialogs

scenarios.title: Run the frozen Linux app without system Python or 32-bit runtime
setup: Extract the Linux package on an Ubuntu 22.04 amd64 desktop fixture with X11/font libraries.
Ensure Python, Tk and the 32-bit loader are absent from the host fixture.
steps: Run packaging/check_package.py against the artifact outside the clean fixture.
Open first-run setup and the Settings shortcut inside the fixture.
Autostart using a private writable asset copy.
Reach the menu, difficulty selection and level 1.
expected: The frozen 64-bit GUI supplies its own Python/Tk dependencies.
The 32-bit child uses the private loader and bundled matching Mesa DRI drivers.
No original game assets are present in the app archive.
Menu and first-level rendering work in the bounded run.

verification.method: real frozen package in a clean Ubuntu 22.04 container

scenarios.title: Run the frozen Windows package without an original game installation
setup: Use the native Windows i686 game and frozen Windows x86_64 launcher in an isolated Wine prefix.
Keep the asset cache outside the application folder.
steps: Open setup and its native file chooser.
Import the supported ISO.
Use the Settings executable and saved autostart.
Reach New Game, difficulty selection and level 1.
Exit the bounded run with F12.
expected: The app resolves its bundled SDL, compiler runtime and decoder.
The launcher and child support the saved Unicode cache path.
No missing original Bink DLL callback is required.
The native image reserves the original data address range before DLL loading.
Physical Windows compatibility remains a separate check.

verification.method: real native Windows program under Wine; physical Windows pending

scenarios.title: Replace a preview app while preserving user data
setup: Complete setup, save a game and record the per-user cache/settings locations.
steps: Extract a new preview to a separate application folder.
Launch the new app with the same user account.
Open Settings and Continue.
Keep the old application available until the check finishes.
expected: Application replacement does not delete user preferences or imported assets.
The existing save is loaded from the game cache or selected installed folder.
A future incompatible settings schema is reported without silently overwriting it.

scenarios.title: Require matching notes before a versioned preview release
setup: Use the committed v0.0.3 release notes and changelog.
steps: Run python3 packaging/release_notes.py v0.0.3.
Run the same check for v0.0.4 without changing its notes.
Inspect the tag-triggered release workflow and versioned package names.
expected: The current v0.0.3 gate exits zero.
The future v0.0.4 gate exits nonzero and asks for matching notes.
Preview status is explicit.
The README releases link includes previews rather than silently selecting an older stable release.

verification.method: release gate commands and workflow review

scenarios.title: Build both apps and publish a complete versioned release
setup: Prepare matching notes and changelog for the new version.
Review the public release text before publishing.
steps: Run normal branch CI and inspect both app artifacts.
Run the approved version-tag workflow.
Check Linux, Windows, proxy DLL, source and runtime-source archives plus SHA256SUMS.
Extract both app archives on clean desktop environments and repeat the first-run scenarios.
expected: Linux and Windows app jobs both succeed before publish.
Archive names and build-info match the version tag.
Required licenses, decoder sources and runtime sources are included.
Checksums cover all downloads.
No copyrighted game assets are shipped.

verification.method: public tag CI and physical install checks remain separate from local build verification

scenarios.title: Extend setup smoke into full gameplay coverage
setup: Use the gameplay scenario registry and legally owned original binary for comparison.
steps: Repeat map-specific spawn, rendering, mission and cinematic routes.
Test punch, kick, web ball, web dome and swinging against actual targets.
Compare visible effects, animations, hit results and progression with the original.
Complete each campaign mission and save/reload its progress.
expected: All maps and attack semantics require independent gameplay evidence.
A launcher smoke, imported archive hash or short key script is never recorded as full campaign completion.
